x: George Beecham won the 2 miles walk handicap with our old friend Harry Shields battling away to gain 2nd place from Bill True, the handicapper!
A good field of 20 Junior walkers, that is junior in performance, faced the starter and a very interesting race followed, with Gerry Warr and George Beecham battling all the way for first position.
At about 8 miles George Beecham had an attack of cramp and fell back considerably. He recovered again at about 9 miles and finished strongly, bettering his county time by 20 seconds.

Congratulations to George Beecham, who walked a steady race and was first man home for the Club. An innovation of the promoters was 12 individual handicap prizes instead of handicap team prizes, and George was placed 10th, to be the only member of the Club to take a prize.
The race opened with George Oliver going into the lead, followed by George Beecham, who was tackling his first 20, Hugh McGreechan, out to hold his title, and George Checkley, all together.
Hugh McGreechan walked extremely well to finish in 3rd position, and George Beecham, by finishing 8th, qualified for his Club Honours Badge.
Nevertheless we finished 4th in the scratch race with George Checkley 13th, Erich Hall 22nd, George Beecham 25th, and Len Demmon 26th. The "A" Team were also 4th in the handicap.
Doubleday 9th (89.29) and Ron Garwood 12th (91.15) made up our team with a score of 24 points to Surrey W.C.'s 26. Joe Wilson, George Beecham, Albert Skinner, another new member, and R.

Their peculiar way of awarding handicap prizes to the first 12 individuals instead of the teams, resulted in George Beecham taking 5th prize, George Checkley, 9th and Joe Wilson 12th, which was quite a good proportion.

Unfortunately George Beecham had to retire and we were only able to finish 4th in the scratch team race with 24 points. This was amply compensated for by the other results, in fact apart from the scratch team race it was a Belgrave field day.
Hugh McGreechan and George Beecham led the field for the first two laps at a very fast pace and one began to wonder who would be the first to crack.
George Beecham gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan the Sydney Bayliss Cup and Bob Newson his first (2nd Class) National Standard medal.

George Checkley was 2nd in the 5 miles, Syd James 2nd in 4 miles, George Beecham 5th in 4 miles, up and coming Ray Middleton 4th and George Oliver 6th in the 3 miles and Len Demmon 4th in the 2 miles.
Hugh McGreechan was 4th with the leading bunch, Norman Guilmant, George Checkley, George Beecham, Harry Shields and Bernard Eglington, in that order, not far behind.
Len Demmon was 2nd with George Beecham 3rd. There were 13 starters and our handicapper, Bill True, with a time of 62m.57s (all.7.15) was second in the handicap with Pot Hunter Harry Shields 3rd.

The backing of Norman and George Checkley, 2nd and 4th positions respectively, gave us a score of 7 points, which must be practically unbeatable unless some club can finish with the first three positions. George Beecham was 9th, Bernard 10th, Fred Rolfe 14th, J.
Our "A" team which also included George Beecham (11th) Fed Rolfe 25th, Doub, 33rd and Joe Wilson 34th, had six men home before any other club had completed their four.
A special handicap was deservedly won by Bob Newson off 3.30 with George Beecham 2nd off 9 mins. and he looked at one time as if he would "smash" the handicap.
Could Eric and Syd continue their good form, and what of George Beecham, Maurice Nye, Bill True and Doub, who was going to make up the team.
Close behind was George Beecham - a gallant performance this after an interrupted preparation, and Norman Guilmant, thinking of something inside eight hours for the "Brighton" next September.
The first six Londoners were to be selected for a visit to Paris and competition was very keen with Syd James, Eric Hall, Bob Newson, George Checkley and George Beecham all in the field.
Bob who was very tired, lost a few places and finished 12th and Norman, 17th, had brought George Beecham along after a bad spell to finish 18th.

George Beecham after battling with Bernard earlier on had sickness near the end of the 2nd lap and retired. Len Demmon trailed the Captain home in 3.13.13 with Bob Readman and Bill True just behind, followed by Cyril Yescombe continuing to show improvement.
George Beecham was well up, too far in fact and eventually paid the penalty. Norman was well up for the Kilos with Bob walking well under control and Harry doing the same.
The handicap was won by Stan Vickers off 2.40. with Denis Ives 2nd and George Beecham 3rd.

Eric's time was 56mins. 18s. with Ted Smith 2nd and George Beecham 3rd. Eric and George both started training under Frank Elson at the Duke of York's Headquarters and naturally were both anxious to get their names on the cup as the first holder.

Eric Hall walked an excellent race in the 2 miles to finish 2nd to R, Goodall in 15 mins. with Ted Smith 3rd in 15.18. George Beecham 8th and H.McGreechan 10th were our scorers in the 5 miles, George Oliver 10th in the 4 miles and R, Newson 6th and L.
George Beecham, competing in this race for the first time, walked an exceptionally fine race to finish 6th in 3hrs. 57mins. 21 secs. and be our first man home.
George Beecham, after his fine effort at Birmingham, improved even further to finish 3rd in 4hrs. 23min. 12secs. and was 2nd in the handicap.

At Croydon Norman Guilmant was 4thm George Beecham, very fit after his holiday 5th, Hugh McGreechan 7th, Harry Shields 20th and Bernard 23rd, with Fred Rolfe, Bert Stallardm Ron Fairman, Joe Wilson and George Oliver coming along behind.
This rather spoilt our chances of a place in the scratch team race as we had to go back to 29th place with George Beecham for our 4th man and eventually finished 4th.

We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.

Noticeable members of the latter pack were Harry Shields and George Beecham, holding a lively discussion on George's latest acquisition in gent's natty waistcoats, a superb creation in green and black satin, but not being worn during the race.

These four were ably backed up by Doub, George Beecham and Ron Garwood and we won the team title by 21 points to 26. Our Middlesex walkers - Cadogan A.C. - gave battle to the might of that County to such good effect that they finished 3rd behind the supplemented strength of Highgate.

A trio of Hugh McGreechan, Bob Newson and Norman Guilmant were at this time some three minutes behind with George Beecham, Harry Shields and Cyril Yescombe completing the team a further 2 minutes back.

George Beecham who took it steady at the start, walked well to finish 6th and Bob Newson over the last four miles, passed Norman Guilmant and really got moving to finish 8th.

George Beecham was obliged to retire with leg trouble. The handicap held in conjunction was really an excellent effort by Bill True, the handicapper, Cyril Yescombe off 28 minutes, winning by one second from Bob Newson, with Syd Spencer 3rd beating Fred Rolfe by two seconds.
Eric Hall retained his title in 56.5.8 with George Williams 2nd and George Beecham 3rd. In the Middlesex event at Parliament Hill Ted Smith finished 3rd.

George Beecham finished 13th with Norman Guilmant 17th and Harry Shields 32nd. Our President tried hard to catch the Woodford man in front of him over the last couple of miles but failed by 20 seconds.

George Beecham 5th and Ray Switzer 13th gave us 36 points in the five miles. From the start Bob Newson and Hugh McGreechan walked a steady race followed by George Beecham and Harry Shields with Fred Rolfe bringing up the rear.
George Beecham following on his good effort the previous week at Birmingham, decided to move into the lead at an early stage and took the prize for the first man to make the turn at Canterbury.
George Beecham, who needs the sun, had to give it best at 29 miles and Hugh McGreechan who had just come off night duty also found it too much and retired.
George Beecham was 7th after overcoming a bad spell in 3.47.37 and Cyril Yescombe who was very strong over the second half, clocked his best time for the distance in 4.55.44.

Our troubles soon started and it was not long before George Beecham was slowing up and we wondered if he would complete the course. A quick check at Coulsden gave us third place and with George not yet fully recovered things didn't look too rosy.

Splendid backing up by Bob Newson, Ray Switzer and George Beecham ensured us of a clear team victory over Leicester W.C. by a margin of 12 pts.
Meanwhile, George Beecham, revelling in the sunshine, came through to fourth with Hugh McGreechan and Bob Newson completing our scoring team in 6th and 7th positions.

We had five competitors in this race and once again George Beecham finished second - his time on this occasion was 4h.20m.50s. With Harry Shields and Fred Rolfe backing up well we won the team race from Polytechnic H. with 17 pts. to 39.

Congratulations to Syd James and George Beecham on their recent marriages. Colin Collis is weakening; having bashed the Club '7' and run quite well he only needs a few well directed words and perhaps he'll be changing in the stable at Windsor Castle again in 1958.

Near at hand was George Beecham (17th) to take over, should it become necessary. Halfway times were not outstanding; Eric and Terry Clark were still leading with Ray Hall in 3rd place closely followed by Cyril Yescombe and George Beecham who were about three minutes in front of George Checkley.
However, form had altered very little for Ray Hall, Hugh McGreechan and George Beecham, 3rd, 4th and 5th last year, filled the first three places this time in the same order!
He capped a grand season by finishing 3rd, followed by George Beecham fifth and Hugh McGreechan tenth. These three occupying the first three places in the Club Championships, held in conjunction.
George Beecham was more restrained than in other years and did not attempt to lead early on but as the leaders were doing over 7½ m.p.h. it was not surprising.
With our police friends we won the match, one of the highlights being the battle between George Beecham and Hugh McGreechan, with George taking 3rd place and the Irish Ash Tray.

George Williams fought out the lead with Misson (Met WC) for 12 miles, at which stage the pace proved too much for George and he faded to sixth place. George Beecham had his usual steady walk to make up the winning team.

Hugh Mc Greechan was almost back to his very best form, George Beecham turned in his usual reliable Championship performance, Jim Morris did splendidly on his first effort, and George Checkley whipped in a really excellent team of eight men.

In the meantime, Ray Hall was holding a good position and George Beecham slowly making up ground. George, who always walks better in the heat, had started off slowly and George Checkley was keeping close to hand.
Poor George Beecham had one of those very rare races (for him) where the distance must have seemed like 100 miles. Between Crawley and Brighton he was forced to drop 11 places.

George Beecham was also a member of the Civil Service team. Ray Middleton was out again on the next Saturday, this time acting as our sole representative in the A.A.A. 7 miles track championship at Hurlingham.

Ken Bailey and George Beecham were also showing good form in the twenties. In the early stages George Beecham, Ken Bailey and Ray Hall walked together, but the pack broke up at ten miles with Ken chasing after the leaders.

Don Bartliff had taken over fourth team position for us, and confirmed that he has all the promise of championships to come in the years ahead; well backed by Ken Bailey, George Beecham, and Will Belderson.
Representing our 'B' team he put two 'A' team men behind him, held George Beecham to one sec., and took the handicap prize into the bargain.

Ray Hall also walked well and by the finish had worked his way into 4th position, so the Bels had three men home before any other team finished one. With Bob Farley 11th, Don Bartliff 13th, and George Beecham 14th, our prospects for the London-Brighton in September look very bright.

At Peas Pottage it was still neck and neck with Vale (S.W.C.) still 3rd with Ken Bailey giving a good account of himself in 5th place, and the rest of the Bels including George Beecham who had been ill with asthma backing up well for team positions.
With Dave King competing in his first ever "Brighton" and George Beecham taking part in only his second race of the year, our walkers were not too sure how the day would go.
George Beecham, who is currently coming into form again, was unable to start through a minor injury. However, thanks to Dave King and Ray Hall we were still able to get up amongst the medals.
Our leading two were now placed 9th and 11th and with George Beecham and John Morris making progress down the field we were certainly in with a chance in the team race.
John Morris caught George Beecham during the second half of the race and these two had a battle right up to the line when they were both given the same time.

A corner to acknowledge George Beecham's solid worth to our walking teams over many years. Again this year he scored in our winning team for the NIJMEGEN Shield (teams of eight), the ninth occasion he has done so.

On a day when half the field couldn't take it we had Ray Middleton (2nd), Ray Hall (5th), Dave King (9th), Bob Farley (11th), Pat Duncan (19th), George Beecham (20th) and John Keown (23rd) - heroes all!
Duncan and King endorsed their placings in the Bath/Weston race and George Beecham was close behind. It was interesting to see Wally Wortley in competition again.

Pat Duncan and that Brighton stalwart, George Beecham, led home our quartet to third place medals at Brighton on September 3rd. Considering that Ray Hall was missing out this year's race and Dave King, after a fine start, was obliged to retire, our performance can be regarded with some satisfaction
Congratulations to George and Marlene Beecham on the birth of their daughter in February.
George Beecham made a welcome return after a long absence with broken ribs and Bob Farley was going better than he has for some time. The less said about the others the better.

For this first time in years Belgrave were without George Beecham who has always been a mainstay of our Brighton teams. If the start was less boisterous without George,Pat Duncan was also strangely quiet.

Pat Duncan, John Moullin and Bob Farley all walked strongly with some secure backing in the form of Dave King and George Beecham. Gerry Cameron had some rude things to say when lapped by one of his clubmates but soon recovered to finish his first 50 Kilos in fine form.

George Beecham moved through steadily to back up our faster men but the real performance of the day came from Bernard Eglinton who not only held George to two minutes but came within an ace of taking the first veterans prize as well.

Belgrave have their share of heroes Tommy Green four times winner, Norman Guilmant won it, L.C.Allen and Harry Shields won the veteran's award, Ray Hall one of six men who have bettered the magical eight hour barrier and George Beecham holder of more winning team medals than any other man.
George Beecham also suffered a bit but those two stalwarts Johnny Morris and John Keown kept us in the reckoning by helping the others through - truly great team men.

Those Belgrave landmarks John Keown, John Morris and George Beecham are still very much alive and will, one hopes shortly be joined by John Johnson.

Dave Debondi had a disappointing race, mainly due to an unfortunate fall in training, ( Lawton still denies tripping him!) but George Beecham's defeat of John Keown should certainly strengthen our chances in the Brighton where both will be fighting for a team place.

Dave collected his seventh winning team medal to equal George Beecham's tally. Bill Couzens presented Club Championship medals to our first three, all gained standard medals, Ron gaining a first class.
